# Hammond et al. (2025) — Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI

> **External, not NASA governance.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary. It never establishes
> what NASA requires, and must not be cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | Hammond et al.; Cooperative AI Foundation, Technical Report #1 |
| **Kind** | Research report (taxonomy of risks) |
| **Status** | February 2025; arXiv:2502.14143v1 [cs.MA], 19 Feb 2025 (p.1). 96 PDF pages. The report states authorship "does not entail endorsement of all claims" (p.2). |
| **Where to get it** | Public: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14143`, confirmed anonymously off-network, 2026-10-26. |
| **Binds whom** | No one. |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** Vocabulary and a taxonomy for risks that arise
when several AI agents interact, which single-system assurance documents do not organize around (our
reading). Useful for comparison only.

**Key content for AI / machine-learning assurance.**
- Identifies three failure modes based on agents' incentives: miscoordination, conflict, and collusion
  (Abstract, p.2; §1.1, p.5; §2, pp.10-19 per the contents list, p.3).
- Identifies seven risk factors: information asymmetries, network effects, selection pressures,
  destabilising dynamics, commitment problems, emergent agency, and multi-agent security (Abstract, p.2;
  §3, from p.20).
- Argues these risks "are distinct from those posed by single agents or less advanced technologies"
  and will not necessarily be addressed by mitigating the latter (§1, p.5).
- Closes with implications for AI safety, governance and ethics (§4, p.43; contents list p.3).

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** None in `../documents/` addresses multi-agent AI risk (our reading).
